acceptanceItems.item: Phase 0 -- real bastrop_tx pack, correctly wired
acceptanceItems.how: New pack `BASTROP_TX` (smartcity-dashboards PR #41): cityKey bastrop_tx, tenant-private, environment staging (no go-live declared -- own later item), generatesFixtures false, jurisdictionFips 48021. Registered in ensureCityPacksTable's durable upsert list alongside the other three packs -- same self-healing pattern, not new architecture. G-11's guard on the literal cityKey 'bastrop' left untouched; bastrop_tx was always a different string, ratified explicitly by decision doc rather than silently relied on. bastrop_tx/staff persona added to smart-files (PR #12), mirroring plan-review's own G-115-item-1 convention exactly -- unblocks smart-files' scopeId=persona.orgId write path mechanically. Embed threading (G-114, cityKey param on plan-review/smart-files embed URLs) was already merged to origin/main but not yet in either checked-out worktree -- synced both before branching.

acceptanceItems.item: Phase 1 -- first real, non-fixture feed (municode public meetings)
acceptanceItems.how: The one real, already-proven feed in this program (municode calendar scraper, G-71) was hard-blocked from ever running against a real Bastrop pack by pack-unaware identity guards (isIdentityHeldClerkHost/assertPublicFeedSourceUrl, from G-74) that refused the real Bastrop host unconditionally, on every pack, with no way to legitimately grant it -- even to the one real pack it exists for. Threaded cityKey through the full call chain (assertCityPackShape -> assertGrantedAdapterShape -> assertPublicFeedSourceUrl -> isIdentityHeldClerkHost; fetchMunicodeMeetings; runMunicodeCalendar; listMeetingsForOverview, including the leaked-record defense) so the hold now fires on every pack EXCEPT the ratified bastrop_tx (omitting cityKey still defaults to held -- refuse rather than guess, matching prior behaviour exactly for every existing caller). BASTROP_TX now carries TEMPLATE_MUNICODE_CALENDAR_GRANT, the real grant object this repo already had built for exactly this purpose and never attached to a real pack. LIVE-VERIFIED against production, not only unit-tested: ran `src/run-municode-calendar.mjs bastrop_tx` against the real deployed smart-files backend (post-deploy) and the real production Neon DB -- fetched 25 real meetings from bastrop-tx.municodemeetings.com, wrote 5 (the script's own limit), including 'Regular City Council Meeting', 'Zoning Board of Adjustments', 'Public Library Board'. Read them back through `meetingsFromPack('bastrop_tx')`: status ok, honesty 'read', recordCount 5. Confirmed template-city is UNCHANGED: `meetingsFromPack('template-city')` still returns status empty, basis 'no municode calendar grant on template-city' -- the identity hold's own purpose (G-74's finding) is fully preserved for every pack except the one it's now legitimately for.

sourceCheckedCorrection: The approved plan assumed the identity-guard fix was a small, one-line change. Reading municode-calendar.mjs in full (not assumed from the plan's own summary) before writing anything found the real shape: isIdentityHeldClerkHost is called from FOUR distinct sites (assertPublicFeedSourceUrl, two places in listMeetingsForOverview including a redundant-looking duplicate check, and the 'leaked record' defense that catches a Bastrop-hosted record surviving under the wrong pack's read path), plus assertGrantedAdapterShape is invoked generically from assertCityPackShape's own validation loop -- meaning the fix had to thread cityKey through the PACK-VALIDATION path as well as the runtime fetch/read paths, not just the obvious two functions. Done properly rather than partially: all four sites now agree.
constraintsHonored: smartcity-os / PermitFlow untouched -- not read, not referenced beyond canon-preamble text.

Additive only: one new pack, one new persona, one cityKey parameter threaded through existing functions (no new mechanism, no restructuring). CODE_BOOKS/AVAILABLE_EDITIONS-equivalent shapes (ADAPTER_KINDS, TEMPLATE_MUNICODE_CALENDAR_GRANT) reused exactly as they already existed.
environment: staging, not live -- no go-live declared, matches the environment badge's own stated purpose and G-115 item 6's precedent.

Secrets (smart-files-api-key, dashboards production DATABASE_URL) fetched from GCP Secret Manager into a local scratchpad path outside any git repo, used only as env vars for the live verification run, never printed to output or committed, deleted immediately after use -- confirmed by listing the scratchpad afterward.
Phase 2 (10 other domains, vendor feeds) not started, not faked with invented credentials or fixture-pretending-to-be-real data.

LESSON: smart-files' Cloud Run service auto-follows 'latest' revision (100% traffic shifts automatically on deploy) -- unlike plan-review, which pins traffic to explicit named revisions/tags and needs an explicit update-traffic step. Confirmed by reading the traffic array before assuming either behaviour; don't assume deploy behaviour is uniform across services in this program even when the deploy command looks identical.

A city-pack-validation-time identity guard (fired from assertCityPackShape's own grant-shape loop) and a runtime fetch/read-time identity guard can be the SAME underlying function called from multiple, structurally different call sites (pack construction/validation vs. live HTTP fetch vs. read-back leak detection). Threading a new parameter through such a guard means finding every call site by grep, not just the two most obvious ones -- this one had four, one of them a not-obviously-duplicate-looking pair inside a single function.
